mappings.note: Both contain the superscription: 'To the choir director. After Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.' (Hebrew text matches Norwegian translation).
Both contain: 'I cry aloud to God... and he listens to me.'
Both contain the full verse about seeking the Lord on a day of distress, hand stretched out at night without resting.
Both contain: 'I remember God and groan... Selah' (Sela).
Both contain: 'You held my eyelids awake. I was restless and could not speak.'
Both contain: 'I pondered the days of old...'
Both contain: 'I remember my song in the night... I search within myself.'
Both contain: 'Will God reject forever? Will he show no more favor?'
Both contain the question about whether his love is gone for all generations.
Both contain: 'Has God forgotten to be gracious? ... Selah' (Sela).
Both contain the realization that the 'right hand of the Most High has changed.'
Both contain: 'I will remember the deeds of the Lord... wonders from ancient times.'
Both contain: 'I meditate on all your works and speak of your deeds.'
Both contain: 'God, your way is holy. Who is a god so great as God?'
Both contain: 'You are the God who does wonders. You made known your power among the nations.'
Both contain: 'With your arm you redeemed your people... Selah' (Sela).
Both contain the description of waters seeing God and trembling.
Both contain: 'Clouds poured out water... your arrows flew about.'
Both contain the description of thunder rolling and lightning lighting up the world.
Both contain: 'Your path led through the sea... your footprints were not seen.'

This verse is present in WLC but missing from OSMAIN (which ends at v20). It contains: 'You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.' This indicates OSMAIN needs to be expanded or this translation includes an additional verse not found in that specific master text version.

extraContent.description: Text: 'נָחִיתָ כַצֹּאן עַמֶּךָ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן' (You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron). This verse is not present in OSMAIN.
